content:
alex: heads-up — noticed customer reported seeing other workspaces' activity rows in the Console activity panel after the routing change last night :eyes:
maria: uhh that's bad. which change? the gateway policy we switched to `prefer-global-read`?
sam: yes that change. we reverted for writes but left read routing global to reduce cross-region hops. reproducer: switch to a user in org A, open Activity, set filter = last 7d, you get rows from org B interleaved.
alex: exact repro steps and query log attached below:
```
GET /api/console/activity?workspace_id=org-A&filter=last7d
x-routing-policy: prefer-global-read
---> upstream service received: SELECT * FROM events WHERE timestamp > ... /* NO workspace_id filter injected */
```
jit: that log means the gateway removed workspace_id when applying the global route — it should never strip tenant scoping. seems like a bug in the router rewrite.
maria: is this an API-layer bug or Console-client passing wrong params?
sam: I inspected network tab — client sends workspace_id header and query param. Gateway v2 rewrite rule matched and rewrote path to `/global-activity` and dropped query param because of a sloppy path-template mapping.
ops-sre: deploy-bot reports the change: deploy-bot: "gateway:rollout prefer-global-read v2 applied to region-us-east" at 1728342000
ops-sre: rollback happened for write paths but read mapping stayed active, looks like a partial rollback.
alex: immediate mitigation: gate the global-read policy with a feature-flag that requires an explicit `allow_global_reads=true` header from Console (so only opt-in clients get it).
jit: I'd prefer server-enforced: disallow a route rewrite that drops `workspace_id` unless target handler accepts `global=false`. Safer to fail with 403 than return cross-tenant rows.
maria: agree. product concern: users saw usage rows that looked like other customers — even though downstream telemetry attribution is unchanged, this will cause confusion and potential legal escalation. We should notify support.
sam: created quick patch to gateway mapping to preserve query params and to inject `x-tenant-check: required` when rewriting. Opening PR: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pulls/1287
alex: nice. also add an integration test that asserts `workspace_id` present in downstream SQL params for all console->activity requests.
ops-sre: also add a hot alert: "activity.nonscoped.rows_count > 0" — fire when we see any event rows returned without a matching workspace scope in the query.
jit: rollout plan: 1) close the mapping bug PR, 2) add test + alert, 3) feature-flag global read off by default, 4) deploy to canary region with sampling. 5) notify support + customers hit.
maria: whom do we ping for support comms? @product-led to draft a blurb, suggest "no data exfiltration, UI-only preview leak" if that's accurate.
alex: can we confirm no PII left the cluster? sam: logs show only activity metadata; no payloads with user content. still escalate to security for triage.
ops-sre: will open incident ticket and attach timeline.
deploy-bot: "deployment gateway:v2.1.14 -> rolled back for writes on 1728343000; read mapping patched 1728347400"
ops-sre: action items summarized:
- sam: PR to preserve query params + add `x-tenant-check` header (in progress)
- jit: update router to 403 on missing tenant filter for console endpoints
- alex: add integration test + regression test in infra repo
- ops-sre: create alert and incident timeline, notify security
- maria: draft support/customer comm with product-led
- product-led: review comm and hold off public statement until security ok
sam: I'm going to ship the param-preserve patch to canary in 10m, will post canary link.
alex: thanks. once canary looks good we can flip the feature-flag off globally and proceed with safe rollout. :lock:
maria: thanks team. please add notes to runbook under Console->Routing as follow-up. :memo:
